#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from PBS
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -g 1 -t 24h --setattr=system.memory=30720M --job-name=QCL_PT script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from select=1)
# -n 1         : 1 task (from ncpus=1, interpreted as 1 task)
# -c 1         : 1 CPU core per task (from ncpus=1)
# -g 1         : 1 GPU (from ngpus=1)
# -t 24h       : 24 hour walltime (from walltime=24:00:00)
# --setattr=system.memory=30720M : 30GB memory (from mem=30GB, 30 * 1024 MB)
# --job-name=QCL_PT : job name/project (from -P QCL_PT)
#
# PBS resource calculation:
# select=1:ncpus=1:ngpus=1:mem=30GB means 1 chunk with 1 CPU, 1 GPU, 30GB memory
# Flux equivalent: -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -g 1 with total memory 30GB

# Original project/account: QCL_PT
# Note: PBS -P directive typically maps to account/project allocation
# Flux uses banks/accounts through flux-accounting
# Set at submission if flux-accounting is configured:
# flux batch --setattr=bank=QCL_PT ...
# Performance impact: Without bank specification, job may run under default account
# which could affect priority, resource limits, or accounting tracking

# Original queue: defaultQ
# Note: Flux does not have queues/partitions in the same way as PBS
# Queue selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux queue policies
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# GPU allocation: 1 GPU
# Note: PBS specifies ngpus=1 (generic GPU request)
# Flux uses -g 1 for GPU count allocation
# GPU type/model cannot be specified in standard Flux syntax
# Performance impact: Job may be allocated any available GPU type
# Consult site-specific Flux configuration for GPU property constraints

# Memory: 30GB
# Note: PBS specifies mem=30GB for total memory in the chunk
# Flux memory specification: --setattr=system.memory=30720M (MB)
# Alternative syntax may be --setattr=memory=30720M depending on Flux version
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient and cause OOM errors

# Module loads
module load cuda/10.0.130
module load openmpi-gcc/3.1.3

# Activate conda environment
source miniconda/bin/activate training

# Change to working directory
cd models/

# Run TensorFlow 2 object detection training
# Direct execution without MPI launcher since this is a single-task GPU job
python research/object_detection/model_main_tf2.py \
  --model_dir="/project/RDS-FSC-QCL_PT-RW/rcnn_model_data/" \
  --num_train_steps=200000 \
  --sample_1_of_n_eval_examples=1 \
  --pipeline_config_path=pipeline.config \
  --alsologtostderr

# Note: Fixed typo in original script: '--alsologtostder' -> '--alsologtostderr'
# Note: The original uses single-CPU, single-GPU configuration
# TensorFlow will utilize the GPU through CUDA
# Ensure CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is properly set by Flux for GPU allocation

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts PBS directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=30720M' may not be correct for all Flux versions. The attribute path 'system.memory' should be verified. Common alternatives include '--setattr=memory=30720M' or the memory may need to be specified differently based on Flux version (e.g., using resource specification in jobspec).

The recommended submission command is missing the bank/account specification. If flux-accounting is in use, the complete command should include '--setattr=bank=QCL_PT' to properly track resource usage against the QCL_PT project.

The script allocates only 1 CPU core (-c 1) for a TensorFlow training job. TensorFlow typically benefits from multiple CPU cores for data preprocessing and loading, even when using GPU acceleration. Consider if 1 CPU core is sufficient for the workload.

No output or error file redirection is specified in the submission command. Consider adding '--output=<filename>' and '--error=<filename>' to capture job output, or the default Flux output files will be used.

The 'cd models/' command changes directory without error checking. If the directory doesn't exist, the python command will fail with a confusing error. Consider adding error checking: 'cd models/ || exit 1'.
The conda activation uses a relative path 'miniconda/bin/activate'. This assumes the script is run from a specific directory. Using an absolute path would be more robust.
OpenMPI module is loaded but not used in this single-task job. This module load is unnecessary and could be removed for cleaner execution.
The script doesn't verify that GPU is actually allocated and visible. Consider adding a check like 'nvidia-smi' before the Python script to confirm GPU availability.
TensorFlow 2 with CUDA 10.0.130 may have compatibility issues. TensorFlow 2.x typically requires CUDA 10.1 or newer for optimal performance. Verify version compatibility.
The absolute path '/project/RDS-FSC-QCL_PT-RW/rcnn_model_data/' is used for model directory. Ensure this path is accessible from compute nodes and has appropriate permissions.
No mechanism to save or check job completion status. Consider adding error handling or exit status checks after the Python command.
